nodes.summary: One linear protocol obligation with its dependency rank.
nodes.title: Endpoint capability with a dependency rank

nodes.summary: The empty ownership map is completed.
nodes.title: The empty ownership map is completed

nodes.summary: A context has no remaining communication obligation. End capabilities may still be recorded, but an active protocol is never silently discarded.
nodes.title: Completed ownership map

nodes.summary: Finite ownership map, indexed by polarized keys rather than names.
nodes.title: Finite endpoint ownership map

nodes.summary: Disjoint ownership remains disjoint when the combined owned domain is rekeyed injectively. Opposite roles are not collapsed to physical names.
nodes.title: Injective rekeying preserves disjoint ownership

nodes.summary: Capability duality does not change rank or lose protocol information.
nodes.title: Capability duality is an involution

nodes.summary: The peer's obligation has the same rank and dual subject protocol.
nodes.title: Dual of an endpoint capability

nodes.summary: Erasing a key preserves absence of any noncompleted obligation; the empty map is not itself a completion claim about hidden ν processes.
nodes.title: Erasing a key preserves completion

nodes.summary: Recording a completed endpoint preserves completion of a finite map.
nodes.title: Inserting a completed capability preserves completion

nodes.summary: Rekeying preserves each capability verbatim at its image key.
nodes.title: Lookups in a rekeyed ownership map

nodes.summary: Rekeying has precisely the image of the original owned keys.
nodes.title: Keys of a rekeyed ownership map

nodes.summary: Completed protocols remain completed under collision-free name transport.
nodes.title: Rekeying preserves completion

nodes.summary: Rekeying that fixes all owned keys retains the exact map.
nodes.title: Rekeying that fixes every owned key fixes the map

nodes.summary: Identity rekeying retains the exact finite map, including end slots.
nodes.title: Identity rekeying fixes an ownership map

nodes.summary: Consecutive collision-free rekeyings compose on the same finite map.
nodes.title: Composition of collision-free rekeyings

nodes.summary: Rekey a finite map when no two owned keys are merged. Global injectivity is unnecessary, which matters for endpoint substitution.
nodes.title: Collision-free rekeying of an ownership map

nodes.summary: Two lookups of the same linear key cannot give different capabilities.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of capability lookups

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
